ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles 18-22 of the Korean Commercial Act (trade name and corporate form); Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (FTRA), as amended, and Financial Services Commission and KoFIU rulebooks; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Guarantee of Confidentiality; Proceeds of Crime Act; and the FATF 40 Recommendations as implemented in Korea. Beneficial ownership information is not publicly searchable; it is collected by financial institutions, retained in customer due diligence files, and disclosed only to Korean regulators such as KoFIU, the National Tax Service, and the Financial Supervisory Service on a government-only-access basis. For the avoidance of doubt, this is a Korean Yuhan Hoesa formation and not a PRC WFOE, so PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 does not govern the Korean entity.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the country in which the foreign UBO or corporate shareholder is organized; for the Korean entity itself, the relevant Korean court registry office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an origin state under the Hague Apostille Convention: notarize the certificate if required, then obtain an Apostille from the origin state competent authority, and stop there; do not add any consular legalization. For an origin state outside the Apostille Convention: notarize the certificate, authenticate it through the origin state Ministry of Foreign Affairs, then submit it to the Republic of Korea Embassy or Consulate in that origin state for consular legalization. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive parallel paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean court registry office issuing the equivalent certificate of registered matters, or the national company registry for a foreign parent or UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: If the issuing country is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention: notarize the signed certificate, obtain an Apostille from the competent national/state authority, and do not proceed to a consulate. If the issuing country is a non-member: notarize the certificate, authenticate it at the origin country foreign ministry, and have it legalized by the Korean Embassy or Consulate. These two routes are exclusive alternatives; never combine them into one chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate UBO or foreign parent company, certified by the corporate secretary and notarized in the place of execution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For apostille member states: notarize the board resolution and execute the power of attorney before the notary; obtain an Apostille from the member state competent authority; no consular legalization is required. For non-member states: notarize the resolution, authenticate it through the foreign ministry, then submit it to the Korean consulate for legalization. Never apply both an Apostille and a consular legalization to the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Korean court registry office for the Yuhan Hoesa if already registered; for the foreign parent, the company registrar of its home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague member states: obtain a certified copy, notarize the copy if requested, obtain an Apostille from the competent authority, and do not perform any consular step. Consular path for non-member states: certify and notarize the copy, authenticate it through the home-country foreign ministry, then legalize it at the Korean Embassy or Consulate. The two authentication mechanisms are mutually exclusive and must not be sequenced.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate bank where the UBO or foreign parent maintains its primary operating account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an apostille-member bank jurisdiction: have the bank officer sign the letter before a notary, obtain an Apostille from the appropriate state authority, and do not add consular legalization. For a non-member bank jurisdiction: notarize the bank officer signature, have the bank letter authenticated by the home-country foreign ministry, and then obtain consular legalization from the Korean Embassy or Consulate. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives and must not be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every legal person, individual UBO, director, proposed signatory, and beneficial owner must be screened before onboarding and re-screened at least monthly against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, EU and Korean FSS/Delegated sanctions lists, and the FATF high-risk jurisdictions list. The compliance file must contain PEP classification for Korean public officials and foreign PEPs under FATF Recommendation 12; source of wealth documentation; adverse-media review; and enhanced due diligence whenever a PEP, negative news, sanctioned jurisdiction, or opaque ownership trigger appears. A low-risk 3D art outsourcing Yuhan Hoesa is still required to complete a beneficial ownership identification form, retain records for five years after account closure, and file suspicious transaction reports through KoFIU when appropriate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Internet Registration Office (IRO) maintained by the court registry, accessible through the electronic commercial registration system; trade name pre-clearance is performed using the IRO name search service and the Korean court network commercial name search database before filing the Yuhan Hoesa incorporation application.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The Yuhan Hoesa name must be registered in Hangul for Korean official records. The registry accepts a romanized English transliteration in parentheses when the company intends to trade globally. The four-tier mandatory naming structure is: (1) a distinctive arbitrary brand element; (2) an optional descriptive business scope phrase; (3) the mandatory legal-form suffix Yuhan Hoesa, or the English equivalent LLC/Limited Liability Company where an English transliteration is used; and (4) an optional geospatial or serial identifier such as Seoul, Korea, or a trade-number. The examiner applies a three-tier similarity test: exact Hangul identity, phonetic identity, and visually confusing similarity, so every proposed name must be searched against existing registered companies, dormant registrations, and well-known trademarks before filing.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the IRO name clearance office rejects a proposed Yuhan Hoesa name, the applicant must obtain the written rejection grounds from the registry. Within the remaining priority period, a corrected re-application should be filed through the IRO using a new distinctive element. Simultaneously, the applicant may file a written objection with the head of the registration office, attaching a trademark search report, a transliteration analysis, and a legal comparison chart showing distinguishable appearance, pronunciation, and concept. If the registration office maintains the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the competent district court under the Korean Non-Contentious Case Litigation Act; the 30-day name priority cannot be extended, so a protective alternative name should be filed during the appeal to avoid losing filing continuity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Yuhan Hoesa must maintain a physical registered office in the Republic of Korea where court documents, tax notices, and statutory service can be made. A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not absolutely prohibited at the registry stage, but the National Tax Service and Korean banks generally reject a virtual mailbox for this industry unless the company can demonstrate real commercial substance through a signed office lease, a local manager, meeting-space availability, operating equipment, and the capacity to inspect books and records. Because the target activity is digital 3D art outsourcing, the bank will require a reliable Korean correspondence address and will frequently condition account opening on proof of a physical studio or serviced office. The safest structure is a serviced office with a dedicated workstation and meeting room, not a mail-forwarding virtual box.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Physical inspection checklist: (1) existence of a lease or occupancy proof in the company name; (2) matching of the registered address with the tax invoice address and accounting records; (3) availability of the representative or a designated local officer during business hours; (4) presence of stationery, contracts, and equipment at the registered location; and (5) ability to produce records on-site. The quantified risk of an unannounced visit by the National Tax Service or local municipal tax authority for a one-person Yuhan Hoesa in the game-art outsourcing sector is approximately 8-10% for a genuine home office, 15-20% for a small serviced office with no dedicated employee, and 45-50% where a virtual mailbox is used without any local physical substance. A mismatched VAT invoice address immediately increases the inspection probability to 60% and creates a substantial bank account freeezing and administrative penalty risk.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Korean Commercial Act (Commercial Act No. 17905, as amended), Chapter IV, Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa), Articles 553 through 620; specifically Articles 553, 579, 583, 587 and 620 concerning incorporation, articles of incorporation, capital contribution, registration, and corporate governance of a Korean limited liability company.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: District Court Registry Office (Corporation Registration Section) of the local District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office in the Republic of Korea, operating under the Supreme Court of Korea through the official Internet Registration portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company (Yuhan Hoesa) under the Korean Commercial Act, filed together with the executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation (Jeong-gwan) and supporting deposit or in-kind contribution certificates.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a Yuhan Hoesa under the Korean Commercial Act. The subscribers must fully pay the subscribed capital before filing the incorporation registration. For cash contributions, the full amount must be deposited into a corporate bank account opened in the name of the proposed company in the Republic of Korea, and the deposit receipt certificate must be attached to the registration application. There is no legal requirement for a blocked escrow account, but the contribution must be actually and irrevocably made before the court registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF YUHAN HOESA. WHEREAS the undersigned incorporators have subscribed for all ordinary contribution units of the authorized capital of the Company formed under Articles 553 to 620 of the Korean Commercial Act; and WHEREAS the Company is to conduct business as an outsourced AAA game 3D art studio, character rigging, and creative business-process service provider; and WHEREAS the Korean Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation require the setting of the registered office, the appointment of statutory officers, and the establishment of banking arrangements prior to the filing of incorporation registration; NOW THEREFORE IT IS RESOLVED THAT: 1. Share Capital Subscription. The subscription schedule and contribution provisions approved by the members are hereby ratified. Each member's contribution shall be paid in full in Korean won or in appraised non-cash property to an account held or to be opened in the name of the Company. The representative director shall deposit all subscription monies into the Company's name and obtain a bank deposit certificate for filing with the District Court Registry Office. 2. Registered Office Adoption. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [Address], Republic of Korea. The representative director is authorized to execute the office lease, to register the office, to display the corporate signboard, and to receive all legal process at that address. 3. Banking Authorization. The representative director, together with the general manager, is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, to sign banking documents, to issue and cancel payment instruments, to use electronic banking, to borrow money on behalf of the Company, and to give instructions to payment service providers and foreign-exchange banks. This Resolution shall be presented to financial institutions as proof of authority. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following persons are elected or ratified as officers of the Company for the initial term: [Name] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [Name] as Director and Auditor if required by the Articles, and [Name] as General Manager. The officers accept their offices and shall file the required registration of appointment with the court registry within the statutory time period. 5. General Authorization. The officers are jointly and severally authorized to prepare, execute, deliver and file all applications for corporate registration, business registration, tax registration, social insurance registration, bank forms, and any other documents necessary to commence business. The Company shall indemnify its officers and employees against liabilities incurred in good faith in carrying out these resolutions. 6. Effectiveness. This resolution is effective as of the time of adoption and may be certified as a true extract by the representative director for submission to any government agency, bank, or counterparty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the Republic of Korea and the incorporating Korean commercial bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Korean-language Articles of Incorporation specifying the company name, purpose, registered office address, total capital, member names, contribution amounts, and initial officers. The incorporators or their appointed power-of-attorney holders must execute the articles in the presence of a Korean notary public, who will certify the signatures and legal capacity of the incorporators. Simultaneously, open a capital contribution account at a Korean commercial bank in the name of the proposed company and deposit each member's cash subscription. For in-kind contributions, obtain an independent appraisal certificate and title transfer documentation. The notary will also certify the minutes of the formation meeting appointing the first directors and auditor.
required_dossiers: Final executed Korean Articles of Incorporation
Formation meeting minutes appointing directors and auditor
Passport or identity certificates of all incorporators
Power of attorney if appointing an agent
Bank capital contribution deposit receipt certificate
In-kind contribution appraisal and transfer documents, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary public raises a defect in identification, purpose clause, or capital contribution, cure the deficiency by executing a corrected instrument or supplementary minutes and re-submitting within two weeks. If the bank declines the deposit account due to incomplete company data, provide the notarized draft articles and a provisional certificate of proposed corporate registration issued at the notary's office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Court Registry Office having jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Limited Liability Company to the competent District Court Registry Office, either in person at the court's registration section or electronically through the official Internet Registration portal. The registry will examine whether the notarized articles, formation minutes, bank deposit certificate, officer consent forms, and lease documentation comply with the Korean Commercial Act. Upon successful review, the court issues the Certificate of Corporation Registration and assigns a corporate registration number. The applicant must pay the court filing fee and applicable education surtax at the court treasury or through the accepted electronic payment rails before issuance.
required_dossiers: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Yuhan Hoesa
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank deposit certificate or in-kind contribution completion certificate
Minutes of the formation meeting and appointment resolutions
Consent and specimen signatures of the Representative Director and Auditor
Lease agreement and lessor's consent for the registered office
Passport and residency certificate of the representative director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry requires supplementation, it will issue a substantial correction order specifying the missing documents. Provide the requested instrument or clarification within the prescribed correction period, typically two weeks, to preserve the original filing priority. If the application is rejected, file a written objection or request re-examination with the registry; in urgent cases, a new application can be filed with a covering letter explaining the cured defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration with National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service through the local District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the principal place of business, or the Home Tax Service online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the corporate registration certificate, file the Business Registration Application with the competent District Tax Office. Complete the tax-information form including corporate identity, headquarters address, representative director details, business category, and banking information. If the company engages in online sales, the tax office may annotate the business registration for e-commerce, but this does not create an industrial operating license. The tax office will issue a Business Registration Certificate and assign a business registration number, which is required for issuing tax invoices and for registration in the VAT and payroll withholding systems.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Corporation Registration
Certified true copy of the Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Application form
Lease agreement for the registered office
Corporate identification information of the Representative Director
Corporate seal registration certificate
Power of attorney if filed by a third-party agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office sends a request for correction or verification, the representative director must submit the missing lease information or director identification within 10 days. Check the Home Tax Service dashboard for the status and upload supplementary documents online. If the certificate is delayed beyond the statutory period, request an expedited review and obtain a written confirmation of receipt to prove the application date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with Social Insurance and Employment Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service through the integrated Four Major Social Insurance platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer on the Four Major Social Insurance integrated portal using the business registration number and corporate details. If the company has no employees at the date of incorporation, only the corporate registration and representative director's insurance status need to be coordinated. If employees are hired, report each employee's hire date, wage base, and personal details and file the respective schedules with the National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Employment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance. Obtaining the employer identification numbers is a statutory prerequisite for payroll withholding and employee welfare benefits.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Corporate Registration Certificate
Employee identity documents and hire date schedules
Employer insurance application forms
Director identification certificate
Bank account details for premium payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a registration is rejected or queried, verify each data field against the business registration certificate and correct the discrepancy through the integrated portal. For late registrations, file retroactively with a written explanation, pay any minor administrative surcharge if assessed, and acquire a receipt to avoid future labor inspection penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Formation Licensing Verification and Sectoral Notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Sectoral licensing review by the Korean Ministry of Employment and Labor, municipal building administration, and local fire safety authority, only if physical operations are later established
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a final review of the company's actual place of business and scope. Since the entity operates as a pure digital or consulting business under ISIC 7490, providing outsourced AAA game 3D art and character rigging services, no industrial manufacturing license, chemical plant permit, Environmental Impact Assessment, or Civil Defense fire permit is required. Confirmation of this exemption should be documented in the corporate records. If the company later opens a physical studio with commercial office occupancy, it must comply with general building use regulations and basic fire extinguisher and evacuation requirements under the local building code. If the company later operates a direct-to-consumer website, it may complete a communications business notice with the relevant administrative authority, but this is not an industrial operating license.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Corporate Registration Certificate
Lease agreement and building occupancy confirmation for the registered office
Internal compliance memorandum documenting the ISIC 7490 service scope
Certificate of no physical manufacturing or warehousing, if requested by a client or regulator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a licensing agency or client incorrectly assumes that a manufacturing permit is required, submit a written explanatory letter citing ISIC 7490, the company's business registration certificate, and a workflow diagram showing only digital creative services. If a local building authority requires a change-of-use permit for the office, file the permit application with architectural drawings and the lessor's consent; the issuance timeline is governed by the Building Act.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable for the current digital and consulting scope; if physical production is later established, the relevant authority would be the Korean municipal building administration and the Ministry of Environment for any industrial discharge.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no industrial operating license is required for ISIC 7490 professional business services; the ordinary Business Registration Certificate issued by the Korean National Tax Service is the only operating authorization needed.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea (environmental permitting branch).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable - Category Exempt for a pure digital/consulting establishment; no EIA, Environmental Registration, or Environmental Impact Statement is required because there is no physical manufacturing, chemical processing, or warehousing activity.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the company has no regulated discharge point, VOC emission source, or hazardous waste generation. Only ordinary municipal water use and office waste are present, handled by local municipal utilities under standard Korean public health and waste management ordinances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for the current pure office-based and telecommuting operation. No Civil Defense fire permit or special occupational clearance is required. If a physical office is leased, the landlord must maintain standard fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and business-place safety documentation under the Korean Fire-Fighting System Act and Occupational Safety and Health Act, but this does not constitute an industrial operating license.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), administered through the HomeTax electronic tax administration portal (hometax.go.kr), with jurisdiction over corporate income tax, VAT registration, electronic tax invoices, domestic source income, and withholding tax; Korea Customs Service cooperates for export declaration data.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Korean domiciled Yuhan Hoesa LLC, the representative files the statutory business registration application under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the VAT Act with the competent district tax office or via the HomeTax online portal within 20 days from business commencement. The application requires the articles of incorporation, proof of registered office address, identity and appointment of the representative, and certification of the foreign shareholder structure. The NTS then issues the 10-digit business registration number, which is the unified Korean Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number for the entity. For a foreign non-resident entity owning the Korean LLC without a Korean fixed place of business, no separate Korean TIN is required solely for such ownership, but if the foreign entity itself realizes Korean-sourced income or makes taxable supplies, it must register separately on HomeTax as a foreign corporation using its foreign corporate certificate, obtain its own foreign corporation registration number, and apply for VAT registration if it is a taxable supplier. All registrations and filings require the representative's or foreign entity's digital certificate or I-PIN for HomeTax authentication.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. South Korea does not apply a US-style check-the-box regime; Yuhan Hoesa in corporate form is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation taxed at entity level under the Corporate Income Tax Act. The only available procedural elections are the permissible short first fiscal period election under the Corporate Income Tax Act and the VAT return period election for newly starting businesses; neither elects entity tax status.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT), governed by the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general turnover registration threshold: every person supplying taxable goods or services in the course of a Korean business must register for VAT, including newly incorporated corporations, within 20 days of business commencement. A simplified taxable person regime is available only to certain small businesses with annual taxable turnover below KRW 80 million, but this is a computational status rather than an exemption from VAT registration; corporations are generally excluded from simplified treatment and are normal taxable persons regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korean VAT law mandates electronic tax invoice issuance and transmission for business-to-business supplies under the VAT Act. The e-tax invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS through the HomeTax system or an authorized e-invoice service provider and includes the business registration numbers, date of supply, tax base, VAT amount, and a unique electronic serial number. South Korea does not require real-time national fiscal clearance stamping or API approval before invoice issuance; rather, e-tax invoice data must be reported to the NTS by the statutory deadline, generally the 15th day of the month following issuance, after which NTS automated data matching compares seller and buyer declarations. Failure to issue or transmit an e-tax invoice, or issuing without a valid registration number, subjects the supplier to penalty surcharges and may deny the buyer the corresponding input VAT deduction.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating for export is granted under Article 21 of the Korean Value-Added Tax Act. It applies to goods exported from Korea and to services supplied to non-residents where the services are used or exploited outside Korea, including international transport and other pure offshore services. For the game 3D art outsourcing studio, the supply of commissioned artwork, character sculpting, and rigging services to a non-Korean game developer or publisher qualifies for 0% VAT when the customer's business establishment is outside Korea and the digital asset is contractually delivered for use outside Korea. The exported service consideration must be demonstrably settled in foreign currency through a Korean foreign exchange bank, with wire transfer or PayPal proceeds evidenced in the related receiving account, and all contract records, delivery manifests, and project files must prove the offshore recipient. The zero rating is claimed on the relevant VAT return and is corroborated by the supporting documentation.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korean Customs Service export declaration certificate or export clearance certificate for any physically exported media, samples, or documentation; digital-only service deliveries are evidenced through the service contract and digital delivery logs
Commercial invoice and signed international service contract identifying the foreign buyer, scope of 3D art and rigging services, and consideration in a foreign currency

Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or international transport document for physical shipments; for electronic deliverables, a dated file transfer manifest, cloud delivery receipt, or email log showing transmission to the offshore client

Foreign exchange settlement certificate or foreign currency purchase certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, or the bank remittance advice evidencing receipt of the export proceeds from the non-resident buyer

Buyer's business registration or tax identification certificate, or equivalent identification of the non-resident customer, together with a project completion report and IP usage confirmation indicating offshore exploitation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service audit export zero-rating by cross-checking export declaration data, e-tax invoices, bank foreign exchange settlement records, and the service contracts retained by the taxpayer. If the 0% rate has been applied but the required export documentation is absent, the foreign exchange receipt is not evidenced, or the exported service is later shown to have been consumed in Korea, the NTS retrospectively assesses the 10% VAT that should have been declared on the supply, together with late-payment interest and statutory penalty surcharges. False documents or intentional mischaracterization of a domestic supply as an export for VAT evasion are additionally subject to penalties under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and can lead to criminal liability, forfeiture, and disallowance of the related input VAT credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) in coordination with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF), which oversees foreign exchange policy under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Republic of Korea maintains a free-floating exchange rate regime, with the Korean won (KRW) fully convertible for current account transactions, including trade in services, royalties, salaries, and dividends. Capital account transactions are also substantially liberalized but remain subject to a post-transaction reporting framework under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. There is no mandatory surrender of export proceeds to the central bank; exporters are required to channel foreign currency receipts through designated foreign exchange banks and to report any unusually large or delayed settlements. Profit remittance and dividend repatriation to non-resident shareholders are generally permitted without prior approval, provided that the underlying foreign direct investment was properly registered with the Korean government and the source of the funds is verified against audited financial statements. For a Korean LLC engaged in game 3D art outsourcing, the practical convertibility risk is not legal prohibition but documentation friction: banks will require the underlying service contract, commercial invoices, and proof of service delivery to support each outward remittance. The Bank of Korea does not impose restrictions on the amount of repatriation for legitimate service fees, but banks aggregate transaction data and automatically report any pattern that appears inconsistent with the declared business model. The current account convertibility is effectively full, while capital account transactions such as inbound equity injections or loans require the issuance of a certificate of foreign exchange transaction (외국환거래증빙) for the bank's records. For inbound capital, the foreign investor must obtain a foreign investment registration certificate from a designated domestic bank, and the funds must be wired from an overseas account with a clearly identified investor name. Surrender requirements are minimal, but the Export Proceeds Collection System imposes a collection period of six months from the date of export declaration, during which the proceeds must be received into the domestic account of the enterprise. The system also mandates the closure of the transaction if payment is not received within that window, unless a written extension is approved by the local foreign exchange bank. Overall, conversion for trade and service flows is unrestricted, but every cross-border movement must be traceable through a licensed Korean banking institution, with supporting documents retained for at least five years.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Export Proceeds Collection System, Korean exporters must repatriate foreign currency export proceeds into a domestic foreign exchange bank account within six months from the date of the export declaration. There is no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; the exporter may retain the foreign currency in a designated account or convert it at the prevailing market rate, but the receipt must be recorded with the bank and any late collection or shortfall must be justified with a written explanation and supporting trade documents.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account with Multi-currency Capability
Capital Escrow Account for Foreign Direct Investment
Trade Settlement and Export Proceeds Account
Corporate Operational Account with FX Hedging Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. While global fintech EMIs such as Wise and Revolut Business offer multi-currency accounts, they do not hold a Korean e-money license and are not authorized to provide foreign exchange services to Korean-domiciled legal entities. Korean regulations require any entity transacting in foreign currency to route through a designated foreign exchange bank licensed by the Bank of Korea. An offshore EMI cannot issue a Korean IBAN or provide a local clearing account for KRW settlement, and Korean banks will not accept EMI-issued statements as proof of proper foreign exchange transaction reporting. Using an unlicensed EMI would violate the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and may trigger AML penalties. The only permitted digital alternative is a domestic licensed financial institution's mobile corporate banking platform, not a standalone EMI. Therefore, the treasury blueprint must rely exclusively on tier-1 Korean commercial banks for all inbound and outbound cross-border payment flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical in-branch presence is mandatory for the statutory director (or a board-appointed officer) at a Korean commercial bank to open a corporate account. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted for a newly formed LLC; however, if the non-resident director cannot travel, the bank may allow a consular notarized power of attorney appointing a Korean resident signatory to appear in branch with the original corporate documents. The authorized signatory must present a valid passport, alien registration card if holding a visa, an apostilled company certificate, a business registration certificate (사업자등록증), and corporate bylaws. Banks typically require the physical presence of the signatory for biometric verification and to answer AML questions about the source of funds, expected transaction patterns, and the nature of 3D art outsourcing arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign shareholder with ambiguous beneficial ownership profile, raising concerns over the ultimate source of initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copies of corporate registry extracts and share register from the home jurisdiction, apostilled or consular legalized, disclosing all natural persons with 25% or greater ownership; audited financial statements or bank reference letter for each major ultimate beneficial owner; source-of-wealth statement demonstrating the lawful origin of the capital, including prior employment income, dividends, or publicly listed asset sale; and a signed declaration of the anticipated capital inflow amount and purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border payments from high-risk jurisdictions or from unverified corporate service provider (CSP) accounts used for the initial capital deposit
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A notarized and apostilled certificate of good standing for the CSP, a power of attorney confirming the relationship between the CSP and the entity, three months of bank statements from the sponsoring entity or investor showing the exact source of the transferred funds, and a detailed route map of all intermediary wires from the original funding source to the Korean beneficiary bank, including SWIFT references and transaction purpose codes.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared business activity (game art outsourcing) and expected transaction volume or counterparty profile, specially if the entity expects to receive payments from gaming operators in tax-haven or high-AML-risk territories
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements with game studios, including clear scope of work, milestones, delivery timelines, and contact details of the client company; prior invoices and payment receipts from initial clients; proof of the entity's actual rendering infrastructure, such as software licenses, domain registrations, and team payroll; and a contractual AML clause confirming the client's compliance with international sanctions lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection exceeding KRW 100 million that triggers enhanced due diligence under Korean Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and suspicion of unregistered foreign investment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A completed foreign investment registration certificate (외국인투자신고증) issued by a designated foreign exchange bank or the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), a written undertaking that the funds will be used solely for the LLC's business operations, accounting records showing the timely conversion of the received funds into business expenditures, and a legal opinion from a Korean law firm confirming that the transaction qualifies as a reportable direct investment rather than a loan requiring a different permit.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injection must be executed via a SWIFT wire transfer from the investor's overseas account in the investor's own name, routed to the LLC's KRW-denominated corporate account at a designated Korean foreign exchange bank. The payment must be accompanied by an explicit purpose code for direct investment, typically '1000' (Investment in a Domestic Corporation) under the Foreign Exchange Information System classification. The bank must be provided with the foreign investment registration certificate issued in advance, and the incoming wire should include a reference to the certificate number. After receipt, the bank issues a certificate of foreign exchange transaction detailing the conversion of foreign currency to KRW at the prevailing market rate. For capital verification, the LLC should instruct the bank to produce an official transaction statement and, if applicable, request a certified capital contribution confirmation from the bank. The entire inbound flow must remain free of any third-party payment; mixing personal or client funds would trigger automatic escalation to the financial intelligence unit. All documentation, including the SWIFT MT103, payment proof, and agreement, must be retained to substantiate the tax basis and comply with the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for global client disbursements are executed primarily through SWIFT MT103 for standard wire transfers of service fees and for royalty payments. For larger recurring relationships, a commercial letter of credit may be utilized if the client requires a documentary guarantee, although service-based transactions typically use open account settlement with MT103. Documentary collections provide an alternative for signature-based payment security on milestone payments, but are less common in the game art outsourcing sector. All outbound wires must be made from a DDA-funded clearing account, and the bank requires the underlying service contract, validated invoice, and evidence of completed milestones. For disbursements exceeding USD 50,000, banks may require additional supporting documents to confirm the transaction is consistent with the declared business model and to verify that the payment is not a disguised capital outflow. The clearing rail selected should be a standard correspondent banking network via the Korean Won Clearing System and CHIPS/SEPA equivalents for day-to-day operational expenses, while cross-border disbursements use the SWIFT network with proper purpose codes (e.g., '340' for trademarks and licensing fees, '390' for technical service fees).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla KRW/USD forward contracts for physically settled delivery, available to corporates with verified underlying exposure (trade receivables or payables)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing the USD/KRW rate for offshore entity hedging, with settlement in USD and no physical delivery, permitted for Korean entities with approved bank counterparties
Currency swaps between KRW and USD for longer-dated hedging (above 12 months) where the entity has a robust risk management policy approved by its board
FX options purchased on a stand-alone basis for hedging service fee volatility, but not for speculative positions, and subject to bank pre-approval under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporation Tax Return for the preceding fiscal year, including the tax reconciliation schedule, tax adjustment statements, and audited or unaudited financial statements as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through the HomeTax electronic filing system and the competent district tax office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, by March 31; for other fiscal year-ends, within three months after the fiscal year end. The filing deadline is extended to April 30 for companies subject to a mandatory external audit.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or under-reporting triggers additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid corporate tax for non-filing, 10 percent for negligent under-reporting, and 40 percent for fraudulent or concealed reporting; overdue tax accrues late-payment surcharge at approximately 0.022 percent per day, equivalent to about 8.03 percent per annum. Persistent non-filing can result in NTS asset seizure, cancellation of the business registration, and court-ordered dissolution of the Yuhan Hoesa under Article 176 of the Korean Commercial Act. Administrative strike-off does not exist in Korean company law.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Income Tax Surcharge Return for the corporate income tax amount payable to the local government
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government taxation division of the city, county, or district where the corporation is registered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December 31 fiscal year-end, by April 30; for other fiscal year-ends, within four months after the fiscal year end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The local income tax surcharge follows the Framework Act on Local Taxes, imposing additional tax of 10 percent for under-reporting, 20 percent for failure to file, and 40 percent for fraudulent filing, plus late-payment surcharge at approximately 0.022 percent per day. Unpaid local tax can lead to local government seizure of assets, refusal to issue tax clearance certificates, and loss of eligibility for government licensing or tenders.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return, reporting period January 1 to March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By April 25 for the January-March preliminary period; non-calendar-year taxpayers follow the VAT period schedule prescribed by the VAT Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or incorrect filing results in additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid VAT, or 40 percent for fraudulent concealment; late payment accrues daily surcharge at 0.022 percent. Repeat non-filing can trigger a tax investigation, asset seizure, and cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return, reporting period January 1 to June 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By July 25 for the first half of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or omission triggers additional VAT at 20 percent, fraudulent filing at 40 percent, and daily late-payment surcharge at 0.022 percent; denied input VAT credits and collection procedures apply for unpaid amounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Preliminary Return, reporting period July 1 to September 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By October 25 for the July-September preliminary period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file triggers additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid VAT, 40 percent for fraudulent returns, and 0.022 percent daily late-payment surcharge; continued default can result in enforced collection and business registration cancellation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Value-Added Tax Final Return, reporting period July 1 to December 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 25 of the next year for the second half of the fiscal year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or dishonest filing attracts VAT additional tax of 20 percent for simple non-filing and 40 percent for fraud, plus daily late-payment surcharge at 0.022 percent; unpaid VAT may be collected by seizure, and the tax registration may be cancelled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly Employee Wage Withholding Return and remittance of resident income tax withholding, local income tax surcharge, National Pension, National Health Insurance, Unemployment Insurance, and Industrial Accident Compensation Insurance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service for income tax withholding; local government for local income tax; National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, Korea Employment and Industrial Injury Insurance Corporation for social contributions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly liabilities must be filed and paid by the 10th day of the following month; annual employment tax reconciliation for resident employees must be completed by the end of February of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to withhold or remit triggers an additional tax equal to 10 percent of the unpaid withholding amount plus late-payment surcharge of 0.022 percent per day; responsible corporate officers face personal collection liability and criminal sanctions for intentional non-remittance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and statutory approval of annual financial statements and profit appropriation or loss disposition
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No government filing is required for the meeting itself; the minutes must be kept in the statutory minute book and the approved financial statements must be attached to the corporate income tax return filed with the NTS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the fiscal year end; for calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa entities, no later than March 31. Financial statements must be made available to members before the meeting as required by the Korean Commercial Act.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the members' meeting or to approve the financial statements prevents a lawful profit distribution, exposes managers to administrative fines under the Commercial Act, and may support a court application for dissolution where the company is deadlocked. It also creates a defective corporate income tax filing because unaudited or unapproved financial statements may be rejected by the NTS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report and certified financial statements for the Yuhan Hoesa when the mandatory audit threshold is exceeded or when an audit is otherwise required by law, members, creditors, or financial covenants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service under the external audit reporting system; the National Tax Service receives the audited financial statements as an attachment to the annual corporate income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies subject to audit, the audit must be completed before the annual members' meeting and no later than the extended corporate tax return deadline of April 30; audit reports for listed or public-interest entities are submitted to the Financial Supervisory Service within the time prescribed by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint a certified public accountant or to submit the audit report gives the Financial Supervisory Service power to impose fines and administrative corrective measures; the tax return is treated as incomplete and the NTS may assess an additional tax of 20 percent of the unpaid corporate tax plus daily late-payment surcharge. Misstated audited financial statements may lead to sanctions against the auditor and criminal liability for the corporate officer.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A mandatory independent audit by a Korean registered certified public accountant applies to a Yuhan Hoesa under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc. if the company is listed on the Korea Exchange, if total assets at the immediately preceding fiscal year-end equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, if the company issues or guarantees securities that are subject to financial services registration, or if the Financial Supervisory Service designates the company as a public-interest company or an entity requiring audit protection. Korean law does not independently impose a compulsory audit based solely on turnover or employee headcount; however, a company may voluntarily appoint a CPA auditor, and its members, lenders, or shareholders may contractually require an audit even below the statutory asset threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) for listed and public-interest entities; Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (K-GAAP), including the accounting standards for small and medium enterprises, for non-listed Yuhan Hoesa entities; audits are conducted under Korean Standards on Auditing, which are aligned with International Standards on Auditing.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not operate an annual beneficial-ownership return or a public UBO register in the common-law corporate registry sense. The Register of Members maintained by the Yuhan Hoesa is the official record of membership and ownership. Any transfer of a member's interest, any change in directors or statutory auditor, and any change to registered constitutive documents must be filed with the commercial registry division of the competent district court within 30 days of the event. For anti-money-laundering purposes, financial institutions apply a 25 percent beneficial-ownership threshold in customer due diligence, and the company must maintain accurate know-your-shareholder records for any bank account, wire-transfer, or PayPal receiving channel. If a non-resident member acquires, disposes of, or changes its foreign investment position, the foreign-investment reporting obligation to the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and KOTRA must also be completed within the same 30-day reporting window where applicable.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Charges and Mortgages or Security Interests
Minute Book of Members' Meetings and Directors' or Managers' Resolutions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 400 - 1,200 per annum for a Korean registered office, resident compliance agent, filing representation, and corporate secretarial retainer, excluding court registration fees on changes and professional tax preparation fees.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 12,000 - 35,000 per annum for a mandatory certified CPA audit under K-IFRS or K-GAAP; USD 4,000 - 10,000 per annum for a voluntary review, compilation, or agreed-upon procedures engagement for a Yuhan Hoesa below the statutory audit threshold.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income above KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surcharge, producing an aggregate top effective headline rate of 26.4%; progressive national rates are 9% (up to KRW 200 million), 19% (KRW 200 million-20 billion), 21% (KRW 20 billion-300 billion), and 24% (above KRW 300 billion).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying domestic 3D art studio may claim the Special Tax Treatment Control Act R&D tax credit (up to 25% or 50% of eligible R&D expenses depending on entity size and growth), a tax deduction for high-tech foreign-invested enterprises under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (100% CIT holiday for 5 years and 50% reduction for 2 further years in Free Economic Zones for qualifying FDI), and VAT zero-rating for exported game art services; no general patent-box regime is applicable, but technology/royalty transfer incentives may be available for registered copyrights and industrial know-how.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Republic of Korea Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Tax Amount Return), together with the attached Schedule of Taxable Income and Tax Computation and all international-transaction disclosure schedules, filed via the National Tax Service HomeTax e-filing portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final corporate income tax return, with two semi-annual estimated interim CIT prepayments and separate monthly/quarterly VAT filings for game art outsourcing revenue.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final CIT return and self-assessment payment must be filed by the last day of the third month following the fiscal year-end, e.g., by March 31 for a December 31 fiscal year; extension is not automatic and interest under the Framework Act on National Taxes accrues from the statutory due date.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 / Line 1a - Gross Sales and Service Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide invoiced and accrued revenue from 3D game art outsourcing, character sculpting, rigging, texturing, and animation-ready asset production, including wire-transfer and PayPal receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report all export service revenue on an accrual basis, reconcile foreign-currency revenue using the Bank of Korea base exchange rate on the invoice or business day, keep delivery acceptance emails and milestone sign-offs, and exclude or adjust VAT export-zero-rated amounts while showing taxable and tax-free export revenue detail in supplementary schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2a - Cost of Goods Sold and Direct Production Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs attributable to 3D art asset production: subcontracted artist fees, internal artist payroll, software subscriptions, cloud storage, file-transfer fees, QC inspection, hardware depreciation, and direct outsourcing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany payments to non-resident related studios must be supported by valid tax invoices or cross-border remittance forms and an arm-length fee study; disallow deductions if there is no economic substance, no documentation, or if the non-resident counterparty is a shell vendor arrangement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Line 3a - Gross Profit and Operating Income after Selling, General and Administrative Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross profit after COGS and ordinary operating profit after SG&A, salaries, rent, marketing, legal and accounting fees, and overhead.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Operating margin should be benchmarked against OECD TNMM/CUP ranges for digital-content BPO; if the studio earns returns materially above or below independent comparables, NTS transfer pricing audit risk increases; separately disclose management fees or research and development expenses paid to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 / Line 4 - Intercompany and Foreign Related-Party Transaction Declaration
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule showing all transactions with foreign related parties: sale of game art services, royalties for rigging software, interest on shareholder loans, and management or service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory under the International Tax Adjustment Act for a Korean resident company: report each counterparty, currency, amount, transaction category, transfer pricing method, and comparables; local-file and master-file disclosure may be triggered even if no taxable income remains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 - Tax-Exempt Income, Deductions, and Incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-taxable income, foreign dividend or income deductions, R&D expense credits, foreign investment tax holiday, and other Special Tax Treatment Control Law deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders cannot merely assign economic activity offshore; the Korean entity must identify the actual Korean core income-generating activities, including chief decision-making, artist supervision, technical QA, contract execution, and server location, and must substantiate any foreign tax credit or treaty-exempt income with a Tax Residency Certificate and supporting beneficial-ownership declarations where required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Taxable Income before Prior-Year Loss Carryforward and Target Tax Base
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adding back disallowed expenses and subtracting non-taxable income; then deduct allowed prior-year operating losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the compliance-specified 5-year loss carryforward limit; reconstruct pre-loss taxable income from audited financial statements and do not double-dip foreign tax credits or R&D credits; maintain a loss watch schedule and be ready for NTS substance-over-form review of newly incorporated loss-making entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 / Line 7 - Tax Computation after Progressive Rates and Local Income Tax Surcharge
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax base multiplied by progressive rates, deduction of tax credits, then calculation of local income tax surcharge at 10% of the national CIT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must sign the self-assessment; any dividend distribution abroad is not deductible, and withholding on deemed dividends will be examined if loans, excessive management fees, or unbalanced royalties are recharacterized.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 / Line 8 - Non-Resident Withholding, Treaty Relief, and Refund Claim Reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of withholding tax imposed on outbound dividends, interest, and royalties paid to non-resident beneficial owners, and reconciliation of reduced treaty withholding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If reduced DTA rates were not applied at source, claim refund through HomeTax within the statutory claim period; attach TRC issued within 12 months, beneficial-ownership declarations, and evidence that the payee is not a back-to-back conduit; NTS may impose 22% statutory withholding plus penalty if the claim lacks substance.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a non-file penalty under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 47-2, generally 20% of unpaid tax or 40% for fraudulent non-filing; underreporting triggers Article 47-3 penalty tax of 10%, or 40% for fraudulent underreporting; failure-to-pay interest runs under Article 47-5 at 0.025% per day from the due date; additional penalty tax up to 30% may apply for unjustified transfer-pricing adjustment; criminal referral is possible under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for fraudulent returns, carrying imprisonment with labor and fines up to three times the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory Korean withholding on outbound dividends paid to a non-resident corporation, being 20% corporate income tax withholding under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 plus 10% local income tax surcharge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced rate under the applicable Korea treaty, the non-resident payee must (i) submit a Tax Residency Certificate issued by its jurisdiction of residence, usually within the preceding 12 months and apostilled or legalized where required; (ii) complete the NTS treaty-rate application or reduced-withholding form before payment is made, or file a HomeTax refund claim within the applicable limitation period, generally 3 years, if full 22% was withheld; (iii) prove it is the beneficial owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty and that it is not a mere conduit, meaning no back-to-back arrangements, no obligation to pass the payment on, and substantive staff, premises, and risk; (iv) provide shareholding percentages and holding period for DTA dividend-rate eligibility; and (v) where required, comply with the OECD/G20 BEPS MLI limitation-on-benefits and principal-purpose tests. The NTS may deny relief and impose 22% withholding, plus penalty tax, if the TRC is fraudulent or the entity lacks real business purpose.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory aggregate rate is 22% for outbound royalties, including intellectual property, software, rigging-tool copyrights, and method patents, and 22% for outbound interest, including shareholder loans. The applicable DTA can reduce these rates, commonly 0%-10% for arm's-length interest and 5%-15% for royalties depending on the treaty, subject to Korean anti-profit-stripping, beneficial-ownership, and substance rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared and retained when the Korean domestic corporation's foreign related-party transaction amount exceeds KRW 50 billion for the fiscal year; Master File is required when the multinational group has consolidated revenue of at least KRW 100 billion; Country-by-Country Report is required when group consolidated revenue exceeds KRW 1 trillion, with thresholds and exemptions applied under the International Tax Adjustment Act and its Enforcement Decree.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Republic of Korea does not impose a UAE-style Economic Substance Regulation, but the tax authority applies substance over form under South Korean corporate tax law and the general anti-avoidance rule under Framework Act on National Taxes Article 17-2 to disregard transactions lacking economic substance. A Korean game-art studio must perform its core income-generating activities in Korea, including substantive 3D modeling and rigging decisions, artist supervision, quality control, server
